page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-32GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 16 vCPUs and 16 physical cores. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-threaded capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is rated in the bottom 10% with a score of 785.99, while the multi-core performance reaches an average tier at 10921.94. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for small-block cached reads at 1073.93 GB/sec but fall into the bottom 25% for large-block uncached reads at 24.65 GB/sec and writes at 19.33 GB/sec. PassMark metrics align with these trends, showing average scores for CPU, memory, and database operations.

Given the shared CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is positioned as a cost-efficient option for multi-threaded workloads that do not require sustained peak single-core performance. It achieves average throughput in static web serving at 11.52 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 23.31 million operations per second. It is suitable for multi-threaded decompression, basic web serving, and lightweight database operations, but is less optimal for memory-bandwidth-intensive tasks or large-scale LLM text generation.
